🔥From Minneapolis to October 7 — When “Resistance” Means Anything Goes

This is an older clip of mine, but the American public needs to have its eyes wide open about how radical parts of Minneapolis politics can get, and how readily some far left militant organizers will exploit a tragedy to push revolutionary goals. With no exaggeration, these are people who openly praise terrorist groups abroad while treating America as morally irredeemable.

David Gilbert Pederson of MN Workers United and Freedom Road Socialist Organization says that during “the four days that the city of Minneapolis was on fire,” they “saw more action in those four days than four years of consistent struggle” against police violence.

He then praises “radicals and militants” who decided the 3rd Precinct was “where they sent their worst officers, their most racist officers, their most corrupt officers,” and says “the community said this shit isn’t safe” so “they burned the pig pen to the ground.”

Then he pivots to armed struggle abroad. He points to the Philippines, saying that as indigenous people are displaced, “more and more indigenous fighters are joining the armed resistance,” and that they in turn are “burning down the worst polluters, the worst military and paramilitary offenders.” (He is talked about New People's Army which is a FTO)

And then he makes the comparison explicit: “that is what happened, collectively, for the people of Palestine on October 7th.”

"Our job is to stand in unconditional solidarity with those resisting oppression."

And he defines “unconditional” as no critique of tactics rejecting “this tactic you did, we don’t really like that” or “I think that some of your methods are too extreme.” “That’s not what an unconditional solidarity means,” he says.

“Our job is not to critique what resistance movements are doing around the world it’s to stand with those resisting.”

The on the ground coalition running the rapid response work is led by the same network of groups Pederson is part of, and several people on that stage are tied into it as well. I broke this down in a full thread last night.

$GRAB Indonesia Region Part 2 🧵

As a part of this small $GRAB retail investor community, I wrote a full thread on this matter yesterday. And I knew bears gonna jump on this so quick. The headline is scary, but the actual implication is wildly different.

This already happened in other regions like Malaysia, Singapore, and the Philippines, where it didnt hurt $GRAB margin, because they adjusted fares, service fee and incentives. You can read the thread and samle below. 

Context: $UBER is getting 25-50% commision, where many countries in SEA are capping at 10-20%. And yet, $GRAB still has higher margin than $UBER due to its massive 2 wheels engine(cheaper Mobility/Delivery and easier to navigate SEA insane Traffic). And 2 wheels is going to be the next massive growth stage for Quick Commerce(Delivery within 15-60 mins); opening the door to e-commerce and more small-medium businesses outside of just restaurants. Will link the thread below

 Most have to consider the impact on smaller players that are burning cash to compete and losing to $GRAB. Because GRAB is already offering insurance on active ride and health benefit in certain respects. Where smaller players can't. This is the final phase of consolidation in the largest market in SEA. And Yes, I do believe this is even maximum pressure on $GOTO to selloff its Mobilty/Delivery segment. 

Before Jan 2026, GOTO Fin Arm was able to charge 146%/year or 0.4% interest a day, now that is capped down to 0.1% per day. The Indonesian govt just devalued $GOTO most profitable arm by 75%. 

If this proposal passed, $GOTO is likely to die in less than 18 months. Or if they pay all debt off, they will only have cash for 3-4 quarters. 

However, this is only a proposal, and I want this to pass as a $GRAB long term shareholder. Meaning $GRAB will be able to buy $GOTO Mobility/Delivery at a much cheaper price tag or it can just die. $GOTO Fin was profitable at $3.7m net income before tax on Q3 2025. This 0.1% interest cap per day will push GOTO back to losing money on its most profitable segment. 

Meaning, $GOTO is going away sooner. I have to assume the negotiation is much more intense from yesterday than 2025. 

I want this proposal to pass. As minor adjustment on fares, service fee, and incentive will keep Indonesian operation at similar margin range. And this is doable because $GRAB ecosystem is the largest in SEA, and they can implement this kind of change fairly quickly, evidenced in Malaysia, Singapore, and the Philippines.

A quick sample of how GRAB would adjust:  
Current policy:  
Ride cost:          $5

Grab earning :  $1  

New Policy if passed:

Most already knew I talked about 70-75% market share overall in SEA, where in Indonesia, GRAB has around 65%-70% market share. I often talk about 90-95% market share in Indonesia or overall SEA. But after this, I  will revise my projection to near 100% in Indonesia if this proposal passed!

Don't believe me? Foodpanda nonstop exit and price war with $GRAB now if you deduct all debt and liability, Foodpanda would have 0 Euro. This business has small margin, and consolidation is happening quicker due to regulatory change. 

When $GRAB gets to monopoly stage, 95-100%, it will do less promos/incentives. It will sell more higher margin services. For example, recent launch of Dine-Out is very successful, with 70-80% margin. $GRAB is also doing GrabMore to accelerate more pickup/grocery, hence we saw much higher transactional growth vs MTUs growth( noted it most of these are done on 2 wheels) 

I expect selling pressure from short sellers and retail investors to continue. "Smart money" will be happy to swallow another 500-700m shares.

$GRAB Today Proposal in Indonesia 🧵

The situation involves a draft presidential decree (Perpres in Indonesian) under review by President Prabowo Subianto, as exclusively reported by Reuters today. This draft proposes sweeping changes to Indonesia's ride-hailing and on-demand logistics sectors, primarily to improve conditions for millions of gig workers to cap Commission from 20% to 10%, mandatory insurance, and social security contribution. 

This is a proposal, not final, and this can change to make it more sustainable for both businesses and gig workers. Gojek last year slammed the 10% suggestion "not a viable solution" or GOTO cannot exist at 10%. Indonesia regulators also recently put a cap on Interest rate where Goto cannot charge 146% a year or 0.4% a day anymore, down to 0.1% a day maximum or 36.5%/year to protect consumers.

Essentially, $GOTO valuation would be 20-30% of current if passed. 

Now for $GRAB, the proposal is estimated to have 30-50% chance of passing with adjustments on these changes. This practically makes $GRAB an employer-like obligation after taking GOTO Mobility/Delivery Segment.

Grab could implement similar strategy like in the Philippines or commission tweaks in Singapore. Meaning fares adjustment with service charges as % to protect margin. This will make $GRAB even more dominance as these changes would make it extremely unlikely for new players to enter. 

$GRAB could also adjust drivers' incentives/bonuses to make the platform more sustainable by switching to perforomance-based. 

If this proposal passed, $GOTO Mobility/Delivery would probably worth less than $700m or potentially just die in a year as it is super unsustainable for Goto to adjust to these changes with a smaller ecosystem and weaker balance sheet and massive debt service. 

With various meeting with the Indonesia President, @AnthonyPY_Tan probably had discussions on this topic. We will have to see how this goes. 

A quick sample of how GRAB would adjust:

Current policy: 
Ride cost:          $5
Driver earning: $4
Grab earning :  $1

New Policy if passed:
Ride Cost: $4.5+ $0.5 service fee (Still $5)
Driver earning: $4(90% x $4.5)
Grab Earning: $1

Essentially to keep everything at similar margin. However, Service Fee as % will be more profitable over the long term than just commission. 

GRAB already offers Insurance to active Trips. This is unlikely to change. It covers accidental death, permanent disability, bodily injuries, and medical expenses arising from accidents during the trip. This is underwritten by partners like Chubb and has been in place for years as an additional layer on top of any personal or commercial insurance drivers might have. It's activated for the duration of rides and at no extra cost to drivers. But this is estimated to be $1 per month per driver for platform like $GOTO, making it even more worthless.

Indonesia govt may subsidize some of the changes to support gig workers through its stimulus. 

I dont think this was the winning bell that Short sellers saw since September 2024. They may claim they saw the future. With that said, I think this is more pressure on smaller players in Indonesia, and pushing consolidation even faster. 

In simple words, this is the monopoly setup for $GRAB to take 100% market share, not 90-95%. 

Alright, that is it. 

Not Financial Advice!

Jan. 14 Santo Niño de Pandacan: The Child of the Pandan Reeds Becomes Pandacan's Mighty Protector.
.
In the early 1600, the miraculous black image of Sto Niño was found by little children playing in the field near a carabao wallow surrounded by Pandan plants. The place was then called Pandanan which means "pandan plantation". The Spaniards mispronounced the name thus changing it to Pandacan.
.
The small, beautiful image is made of wood that is strikingly similar to the dark Mexican wood of the images of the Black Nazarene of Quiapo and the Black Madonna of Antipolo. It is thought that it may have been part of the cargo carried by a ship plying the galleon trade between Manila and Acapulco, Mexico, during the Spanish colonial period. A storm that frequently disturbs the Pacific Ocean may have sunk or destroyed the galleon, and the currents may have swept the image into the Pasig River leading to one of its arteries in Pandacan, which was then part of the parish of Sampaloc.
.
Since Pandacan at that time was still part of the parish of Sampaloc, the elders of Pandacan had the image enshrined at Sampaloc Church. After some time, however, the image inexplicably disappeared from Sampaloc only to be found in the same place where it had been first seen in Pandacan. When it was brought back to Sampaloc church, it disappeared the second time only to be found on the very same spot where it was originally discovered.
.
Believing that the miraculous image wanted a home in Pandacan, the elders of the barrio, together with the Franciscan Priests of Sampaloc, decided to build a Visita (nipa hut) to enshrine the image. The Visita was constructed on the very spot where the Holy image was found.
The water hole frequented by carabaos (a swamp-type domestic water buffalo found in the Philippines) was eventually turned into a well, where a natural spring thrives to this day. Eventually, the Franciscan friars and the townsfolk had a stone chapel built on the hallowed spot, also incorporating the well. This was finished in time for the formal creation of the parish of Pandacan in 1712, when the district was ecclesiastically separated from the Loreto Church of Sampaloc. The water from the well has been instrumental in many miracles.
.
In 1896, the Spanish authorities learned that Pandacan was the meeting place of the revolutionaries. Pandacan was decreed to be ruled under the “Juez de Cuchillo,” meaning the town would be bombed. When the cannons were brought in Nagtahan and aimed at the church, a small child was seen on top of the cannon. The commander, dreadfully struck, suspended the almost certain annihilation of the parishioners.
.
In 1911, Fr. Silvino Manalo placed the Santo Niño at the church tower’s window facing the maddening fire approaching Pandacan. The wind changed its course and Pandacan was saved from a great conflagration.
.
On December 18, 1941, the late parish priest Rev. Fr. Teodoro Francisco, fearing the possible explosion of Pandacan due to the oil tanks and depot ignited by the United States Army Forces in the Far East (USSAFE) before retreating to Bataan, tried to secure the image of Santo Niño but it could not be removed from its pedestal. The feared explosion did not happen and Pandacan was once again spared.
.
The original stone chapel was destroyed by powerful earthquakes in the 1800s. The renovated structure and the well, which existed until the early years following World War II, had to be demolished because of the expansion of Jesus Street into a major road. It was revived sometime between 1951 and 1971 when Msgr. Guillermo Mendoza was the parish priest.
.
The wooden image of the Sto. Niño remained enshrined in the stone chapel even after the church that took nearly 30 years to build was finished in 1760. It was only transferred permanently to the church in 1906 when the church compound and the convent, taken over by revolutionary priests of the Iglesia Filipino Independiente (the Philippine Independent Church, more commonly known as the Aglipayan Church) in 1902, were legally reclaimed by the Archdiocese of Manila.
.
Many miracles and healing of the sick were received and witnessed by the faithful because of their fervent call to the Most Holy Child Jesus and the water from the well of the Holy Image. Devotion to the miraculous image of Sto. Niño de Pandacan grew and became so popular, captivating the heart of everyone. He in turn showered his devotees with graces and became its protector from peril.
